texts.setting.arcade_license.about: For Xbox Live Arcade games only. An Arcade game and its free trial are the same file: the game asks the console whether it was bought. "full" answers yes, and the whole game can be played. "trial" answers no, and the game is its trial version. A game from a disc image is not affected. This setting is part of the console: a movie made with one does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.break_on_unimplemented_instructi: Xenia's break_on_unimplemented_instructions. When the game's code has an instruction Xenia cannot translate, the game stops there. Off, the instruction is passed over, and some games then run on. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.cl.about: Xenia's cl: words handed to the game as its command line, as a development kit could. Gears of War 2 and 3 skip their opening films with "-NoStartupMovies". Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.clear_memory_page_state.about: Xenia's clear_memory_page_state. Xenia keeps track of which pages of the console's memory the graphics chip wrote; this marks them again every frame, so that the next draw sees what was written there. It fixes models that are missing or warped in some games, Team Ninja's among them, and costs some speed. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.cpu_speed.about: How fast the console's processor is: how many million instructions it runs in a second, counting all six of its threads together. 2000, the default, is the closest to a real console, and the speed games are made for: some do not finish loading at all below it (Prince of Persia Classic stays on "Now loading..." for ever at 500 and at 1000). Many games keep the processor busy even while they wait for the next frame, so your computer has to run about this many instructions for every second of the game, and it manages a few hundred million: at 2000 such a game runs at about a quarter of full speed, at 1000 half, at 500 near full speed. 500 and 1000 suit a game that loads at them, when speed matters more while making a TAS; 4000 is for a game that is still too slow. This setting is part of the console: a movie made at one speed does not play back at another.
texts.setting.depth_bias_shader_offset.about: Xenia's depth_bias_shader_offset. Decals that a game draws a tiny distance in front of a surface are moved by the shader rather than by the graphics card's fixed depth bias, which cannot reproduce such small values. It fixes flickering decals. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It changes only the picture: nothing the graphics card draws goes back into the console's memory, so a movie plays back with either value.
texts.setting.force_depth_clamp.about: Xenia's force_depth_clamp: what lies in front of the near plane or behind the far one is clamped to it rather than cut away, where the game asks for clipping. The graphics card must support depth clamping. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It changes only the picture: nothing the graphics card draws goes back into the console's memory, so a movie plays back with either value.
texts.setting.gamma_render_target_as_unorm16.a: Xenia's gamma_render_target_as_unorm16. Where the graphics card cannot blend the console's gamma-encoded 8-bit targets directly, they are kept at 16 bits a channel so that blending is right; off keeps them at 8, which is faster and less exact. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It changes only the picture: nothing the graphics card draws goes back into the console's memory, so a movie plays back with either value.
texts.setting.gpu_allow_invalid_upload_range.a: Xenia's gpu_allow_invalid_upload_range: the graphics chip may read from pages of the console's memory that are marked as not to be read. Some games need it to draw at all. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.ignore_offset_for_ranged_allocat: Ranged Allocations at the Range's Start

Xenia's ignore_offset_for_ranged_allocations. Memory a game asks for within a given range starts exactly at the range's lowest address, without the 4 KiB Xenia otherwise leaves; some games check that it does. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.launch_module.about: Xenia's launch_module: the program on the disc that is started, instead of default.xex. Assassin's Creed III and IV are started from "scimitar_final.xex". Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.mount_scratch.about: Xenia's mount_scratch: the console's scratch partition is there for the game to use, as on a console with a hard drive. Some games keep something on it, such as an instant replay, or will not start without it. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.occlusion_query.about: Xenia's occlusion_query: how the console's question "how many pixels of this were visible?" is answered, for lens flares, culling and the like. "fake" answers with a made-up count (Occlusion Answer, Lowest and Highest) without asking the graphics card, the same on every computer. "strict" asks the card and waits for the answer. "fast" and "fast-alt" do not wait, and their answer can depend on how far the card had got even on one card: for a movie, use "strict". It makes the console's memory hold what your graphics card draws: a movie made with it may play back differently on another graphics card or driver, and does not play back with the null renderer. The New Project window never sets it by itself; Xenia Manager's optimized settings name it in the note when they use it for the game (user-decided, 2026-10-16).
texts.setting.occlusion_query_fake_lower_thres: Xenia's occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold. A game asks how many pixels of something were visible (an occlusion query) for lens flares, culling and the like. This core never asks the graphics card, so that the console is the same on every computer: it answers with a made-up count between this number and the next setting's. -1 answers nothing, and some games then wait for good. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.occlusion_query_fake_upper_thres: Xenia's occlusion_query_fake_upper_threshold: the highest made-up count, see Occlusion Answer, Lowest. Keep it at or above that one. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.occlusion_query_full_counters.ab: Xenia's occlusion_query_full_counters: the occlusion query also counts the pixels that failed the depth and stencil tests, in the shader, for the few games that ask. It matters only when Occlusion Query asks the graphics card. It makes the console's memory hold what your graphics card draws: a movie made with it may play back differently on another graphics card or driver, and does not play back with the null renderer. The New Project window never sets it by itself; Xenia Manager's optimized settings name it in the note when they use it for the game (user-decided, 2026-10-16).
texts.setting.pads.about: How many controllers are plugged in, from the first port. A game sees the other ports as empty.
texts.setting.protect_zero.about: Xenia's protect_zero: the console's first page of memory can be neither read nor written, as on the console, so a game that reads through a null pointer stops there. Some games read it by mistake and run only with this off. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.readback_memexport.about: Xenia's readback_memexport: what a game's shaders write into memory on the graphics card is copied back into the console's memory, for the few games that read it there (Xenia Manager's list names Splinter Cell: Conviction and Blacklist). It waits for the graphics card at every such draw and is slow. It makes the console's memory hold what your graphics card draws: a movie made with it may play back differently on another graphics card or driver, and does not play back with the null renderer. The New Project window never sets it by itself; Xenia Manager's optimized settings name it in the note when they use it for the game (user-decided, 2026-10-16).
texts.setting.readback_resolve.about: Xenia's readback_resolve: whether what a game draws into a texture is copied back into the console's memory, for the games that read it there (Max Payne 3's picture is black without it). "none" copies nothing, "full" waits for the graphics card at every copy and is slow, "fast" reads the copy made a frame before; in this core "fast" also waits for that copy, so a run is the same every time on one graphics card. It makes the console's memory hold what your graphics card draws: a movie made with it may play back differently on another graphics card or driver, and does not play back with the null renderer. The New Project window never sets it by itself; Xenia Manager's optimized settings name it in the note when they use it for the game (user-decided, 2026-10-16).
texts.setting.render_target_path_vulkan.about: Xenia's render_target_path_vulkan: how the console's render targets are drawn. "fbo" uses the graphics card's own targets and blending, copying between them where needed: fast, and less exact with some pixel formats. "fsi" does the console's blending and depth tests in the pixel shader, which is exact but slower and needs a card with fragment shader interlock; without it Xenia uses "fbo". It changes only the picture: nothing the graphics card draws goes back into the console's memory, so a movie plays back with either value.
texts.setting.renderer.about: How the picture is drawn. "vulkan-hw" is Xenia's Vulkan renderer on your computer's graphics card, through the Vulkan bridge. "null" draws nothing: the game runs exactly the same, with a black picture, and needs no graphics card. Nothing the graphics card draws goes back into the console's memory, so a movie made with one plays back with the other.
texts.setting.scribble_heap.about: Xenia's scribble_heap: memory a game is given is filled first, with the byte of Fill Value. Some games that read memory before writing it run only so. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.scribble_heap_value.about: Xenia's scribble_heap_value: the byte Fill New Memory writes, 1 to 255. 0 fills it with numbers from the console's own sequence of random numbers, the same on every run. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.use_dedicated_xma_thread.about: Xenia's use_dedicated_xma_thread: the compressed sound is decoded on a thread of its own. Off, it is decoded when the game asks, which fixes the sound of some games. Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.setting.xma_decoder.about: Xenia's xma_decoder: which of Xenia's decoders turns the console's compressed sound (XMA) into samples. "new" is the current one, "old" the one before it, "master" the one of the original Xenia, "fake" decodes nothing and is silent. Some games play their sound right only with "old". Xenia Manager's optimized settings suggest it for some games, and the New Project window sets it when it knows the game. It is part of the console: a movie made with one value does not play back with the other.
texts.slot.content.help: Packages to put in the console's storage before the game starts, as standalone Xenia's File > Install Content does: add-on content (DLC), title updates and saved games. Each is one file as it sits in the console's storage under Content/<profile>/<title>/<kind>: add-on content and saved games have a long name of letters and digits and no extension, and a title update's name starts with TU_ and has a dot in it. Add-on content and title updates are used as they are; a saved game is unpacked into the storage and is the machine's from then on. The project and the movie record exactly which files were used, as they do for the game.
texts.slot.game.help: The game: a disc image (.iso) of an Xbox 360 game disc, or an Xbox Live Arcade game. A game on several discs takes every disc, in order: the first is started, and the others are put in when the game asks for them. An Arcade game is one file with no extension and a long name of letters and digits, as it sits in the console's storage under Content/0000000000000000/<title>/000D0000. Games on Demand (a small file beside a folder of data files) are not supported. The console's own system software is not needed: Xenia stands in for it. Xenia Canary's compatibility list (github.com/xenia-canary/game-compatibility) says which games work.
texts.slot.savedata.help: What the console kept, as Emulator > Export Save Data... wrote it: a .zip whose entries are all under content/ (profiles and saved games). It is put back in the console's storage before the game starts. A saved game as a single package from a console goes in the Content slot instead.
